blocks.content: The Prime Meridian at 0° longitude passes through Greenwich, London, and serves as the primary reference line for global time zones and east-west positional measurement.

rows: Semi-circle of equal length to all meridians

items: Indian Standard Time (IST) is calculated from 82.5° E longitude (passing near Prayagraj) and is exactly 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of the Prime Meridian (GMT +5:30).
Exams frequently test the 8 countries traversed by the Prime Meridian: UK, France, Spain, Algeria, Mali, Burkina Faso, Togo, and Ghana.
Remember that lines of longitude (meridians) converge at the poles, unlike lines of latitude (parallels) which remain equal distance apart.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Prime Meridian is the 0° longitude line used as the international reference point for measuring geographic longitude.
It passes through the Royal Observatory at Greenwich, London, establishing Greenwich Mean Time (GMT).
Together with the 180th meridian, it divides the Earth into the Eastern and Western Hemispheres.
It intersects the Equator at 0° latitude, 0° longitude in the Gulf of Guinea in the Atlantic Ocean.
It crosses eight countries: United Kingdom, France, Spain, Algeria, Mali, Burkina Faso, Togo, and Ghana.
